problem: Step 6 answers 'Safe and idempotent: GET, PUT and DELETE', which lumps the two properties together and contradicts Section 2, where PUT and DELETE are explicitly called not safe because they change state. A student copying this into an exam would wrongly claim PUT and DELETE are safe.
fix: Safe: GET only. Idempotent: GET, PUT and DELETE. POST is neither safe nor idempotent. State the two lists separately.

problem: PATCH is listed in the method table in Section 1 but is never classified here, so a student cannot tell whether PATCH is safe or idempotent. In general PATCH is not guaranteed idempotent, and it is not safe.
fix: Add one line: PATCH is not safe, and it is not guaranteed idempotent, because the patch document may describe a change relative to the current value (for example 'increment stock by 1').

problem: 'A method is safe if it does not change server state' is loose. Servers do change state on every call (logs, counters, audit rows); safety is about whether the client asks for a change of the resource.
fix: Say: a method is safe if the client is not asking the server to change any resource; GET is safe, even though the server may still write a log line.
